claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 faithfully captures 29 CFR 1910.132(a), including the full scope of environmental and process hazards and the required condition and maintenance of protective equipment.
Claim C0001 faithfully represents 29 CFR 1910.132(b) concerning employer responsibility for employee-owned protective equipment.
Claim C0002 accurately conveys the safe design and construction requirement of 29 CFR 1910.132(c).

Paragraph (g) explicitly restricts paragraph (d) to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, while expressly excluding §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. Because C0003 omits this governing scope limitation from both its explicit scope and summary, its reading is overbroad and admits hazard assessments for respiratory or electrical equipment that the source excludes.

While C0004 includes the lead-in condition from paragraph (d)(1), it fails to incorporate the overarching restriction from paragraph (g) limiting paragraph (d) duties to specific subpart standards and excluding §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137, making the scope and summary overbroad.

Claim C0005 omits the governing limitation of paragraph (g) that restricts paragraph (d) requirements to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, resulting in overbroad scope and summary.

Claim C0006 omits the governing limitation in paragraph (g), which restricts paragraph (d) equipment fitting obligations and explicitly excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137, rendering the scope and summary overbroad.
Claim C0007 accurately states the advisory reference to non-mandatory appendix B under paragraph (d)(1).

Claim C0008 captures the written hazard assessment certification elements but omits the governing scope limitation of paragraph (g), which restricts paragraph (d) certification obligations to the designated subpart standards and excludes respirators and electrical PPE.
Claim C0009 faithfully captures the prohibition on using defective or damaged PPE in 29 CFR 1910.132(e).

Claim C0010 asserts an unqualified employer duty to train employees required by § 1910.132 to use PPE, omitting the governing restriction from paragraph (g) that limits paragraph (f) duties to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, and excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137.

Claim C0011 details the five training topics but omits the governing limitation of paragraph (g) restricting paragraph (f) training requirements, causing scope and summary to be overbroad across excluded PPE standards.
Claim C0012 omits paragraph (g)'s restriction governing paragraph (f), overextending the employee demonstration requirement to PPE outside the covered standards.

Claim C0013 captures the retraining circumstances in paragraph (f)(3) but fails to incorporate the overarching limitation in paragraph (g), which restricts paragraph (f) and excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137.
Claim C0014 correctly captures the cross-subpart applicability and exclusions set out in 29 CFR 1910.132(g).
Claim C0015 accurately states the general employer-payment obligation in 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(1), including its cross-reference to exceptions (h)(2) through (h)(6).
Claim C0016 faithfully represents the non-specialty footwear and prescription eyewear payment exception in 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(2), including the off-site permission proviso.
Claim C0017 accurately conveys the reimbursement exemption for built-in metatarsal protection in 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(3).
Claim C0018 accurately captures the payment exemption for logging boots specified in 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(4)(i).
Claim C0019 correctly conveys the payment exemption for everyday clothing under 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(4)(ii).
Claim C0020 faithfully reflects the payment exemption for ordinary clothing and items used solely for protection from weather under 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(4)(iii).
Claim C0021 correctly preserves the replacement PPE payment obligation and its employee loss/intentional damage exception under 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(5).
Claim C0022 accurately represents the permission and non-reimbursement rule for employee-owned protective equipment under 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(6).
Claim C0023 accurately captures the prohibition against requiring an employee to provide or pay for PPE unless excepted, pursuant to 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(6).
Claim C0024 preserves the effective date and implementation deadline specified in 29 CFR 1910.132(h)(7).
Claim C0025 accurately represents the priority rule in the Note to § 1910.132(h) where another OSHA standard specifies payment requirements.
